## Also fix in the next fix round: this PR breaks its own bookkeeping

Besides the Codex P1 finding, there is a second problem. It is not reported as a review thread.

**What happens:** the `bookkeeping` check on head `4fffef7` failed ([run 38535949966](https://github.com/LauraMardones/headless-pr-workflow/actions/runs/38535949966)) with:

```
hpw: error: unrecognized arguments: --errors-file /home/runner/work/_temp/bookkeeping-errors.json
```

**Why:** for a `pull_request_review` event, GitHub runs the workflow file from this PR's branch. The job, though, checks out `main` (`ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}`) and runs `main`'s `hpw`. This PR's workflow passes `--errors-file`, and `main`'s `hpw` doesn't have that option, so the job exits with code 2.

**Consequence:** Codex's review of `4fffef7` was not recorded, and #330 stayed in "In review" until the PO ran the job by hand from `main` ([run 38537402626](https://github.com/LauraMardones/headless-pr-workflow/actions/runs/38537402626)). Every later Codex review of this PR that arrives as a PR review fails the same way, so the story gets stuck again after the fix round.

`issue_comment` runs are not affected, because they use `main`'s workflow file. After merge, the workflow and the code are both on `main` and agree again. The problem exists only while the PR is open, but that is exactly when its review must be recorded.

**What the fix needs:** a workflow from this branch must keep working with `main`'s `hpw` until merge. Two ways to get there:

- pass `--errors-file` only when the installed `hpw codex-review-bookkeeping` accepts it, and skip the notify step when there is no errors file; or
- split the change, so the `hpw` option lands on `main` first and the workflow starts using it in a later PR.

Add a test that fails when the workflow passes an option the default-branch `hpw` does not have. Or, if that is not practical, record in the PR why the chosen way is safe during the transition.

Related, in Codex's P1 finding: runs triggered by `pull_request_review` are recorded under the PR's head branch, not the default branch. `fetch_history()` has to include them.
